answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens to audit peer interaction graphs via topological cut verifications. A sparse cut acts like a severed vine, exposing colluding clusters that fail game-theoretic cross-validation. Staked timber assets are slashed when audit consensus detects fabricated identities, while legitimate agents climb a tiered terrace of verified reputation. Manufacturing fake subgraphs yields superlinear attacker cost scaling with network size.
